heading: How to Calculate Your Term Insurance Cover: A Practical Guide
tldr: Relying solely on a 10-15 times annual income rule for term insurance cover is often insufficient for comprehensive financial planning.
A robust calculation must account for all outstanding liabilities, future financial goals like children's education, and dependents' ongoing living expenses.
Inflation significantly erodes the purchasing power of money over time, necessitating a higher cover amount to meet future needs.
Any existing assets, investments, and current life insurance policies can be factored in to reduce the net term insurance required.
Regularly reviewing your term insurance cover is crucial as life stages, income, and financial responsibilities evolve.
caption:
Thinking about term insurance? Don't just pick a random number. Your family's future needs, like your kids' schooling and daily expenses, will change over time, and inflation can make money worth less. This simple guide helps you figure out the right amount so your loved ones are truly protected. Read the full article to learn how.
